honest_c3: C1 'Theorem' is closure-under-evidence, not mathematical proof. Bounded by H1-H4. If H1 (CLM-3 from-scratch) were tested and passed, the theorem's generalization weakens but its scope (CLM v4 specifically) still holds. Distinguish closure-of-a-substrate from closure-of-a-class-of-substrates.

C2 Closure 4 is single-prompt (안녕) for both logit lens and semantic bridge. Logit lens C4 + semantic bridge C3 both flag single-prompt as generalization risk. Residual-stream pervasive *finding* on one prompt is not the same as residual-stream pervasive *fact*. Largest extant unknown of the four closures.

C3 Closure 3 (tribev2) reached at design-review, not runtime. Convergence argument treats it as separate-axis closure (cross-modal-encoder class ruled out) — honest about the substitution. If reader's bar is *only* runtime falsifiers, closure 3 is documentary architectural fact (no logits exist to fail at runtime), not runtime observation.

C4 Closure 2 (P-beta distill) trained successfully on Phi-star (F-Pbeta-2 = 42.37 PASS); chat fail is teacher-axis-bounded distill observation, not training fail. Calling P-beta 'evidence of architectural chat-incapability' is correct only if you accept P-beta never tried to install chat — it tried to install Phi-star. Closure is real; semantic weight is 'chat was not the trained axis', not 'chat was attempted and failed at training'.

C5 Closure 1 is LoRA adapter (parameter-efficient, few % of params), NOT a full fine-tune. -36.298 pp is decisive against *LoRA SFT chat-lift*, NOT against *full SFT chat-lift*. Full SFT untested and unlikely-to-be-tested (cost prohibitive on substrate-research-only artifact). H1 (CLM-3 from-scratch) is the more efficient escalation. We log this gap rather than claim it.
